# RATIÉ CH. 3 — THE ABSOLUTE SUBJECT (the heart of the treatise, ĪPK 1.3.7)
*Per-chapter analysis for the thesis. Source lines 8573–12230. The core positive claim:
the unifier of all cognitions is the one consciousness "Maheśvara," with the three powers.*

---

## 1. THE CHAPTER'S THESIS
The kārikā 1.3.7 — "the heart of the treatise" — names the one consciousness that unifies
all cognitions, possessing the powers of **jñāna (knowledge), smṛti (memory), apohana
(exclusion)**. Sovereignty (aiśvarya) = freedom (svātantrya). This is the bearer that the
whole thesis recognizes.

## 2. ⚠️ THE CORRECTION (verified against the actual text)
The three powers of ĪPK 1.3.7 are **jñāna–smṛti–apohana**, NOT icchā/jñāna/kriyā.
Verified in both the IPK text and Ratié Ch3 (lines 8591–8596, 8741). The icchā/jñāna/kriyā
triad is the prefatory/structural reading, not 1.3.7.

## 3. EXTENDED QUOTES (French verbatim + English translation)

### Q1 — The kārikā itself (lines 8591–8596)
> "na ced antakṛtānantaviśvarūpo maheśvaraḥ / syād ekaś cidvapur jñānasmṛtyapohanaśaktimān
> // … S'il n'existait pas un unique Grand Seigneur… possédant les pouvoirs (śakti) de
> connaissance (jñāna), de mémoire (smṛti) et d'exclusion (apohana)."
> **"If there did not exist a unique great Lord… possessing the powers (śakti) of knowledge
> (jñāna), memory (smṛti) and exclusion (apohana)."**

### Q2 — The unifier resolves the Buddhist problem (lines 9259–9269)
> "la kārikā I, 3, 7 permet de résoudre le problème que la théorie bouddhique laissait en
> suspens… la 'souveraineté' (aiśvarya) n'est rien d'autre que la liberté ou l'autonomie."
> **"the kārikā I, 3, 7 allows solving the problem the Buddhist theory left hanging… the
> 'sovereignty' (aiśvarya) is nothing other than freedom or autonomy."**

**→** The synthesis (Ch2) requires a unifier = Maheśvara; his essence is freedom.

### Q3 — The triad of the Pratyabhijñā (lines 8738–8742, note)
> "la triade caractéristique de la Pratyabhijñā 'connaissance, mémoire, exclusion'
> (jñānam smṛtir apohanam)."
> **"the triad characteristic of the Pratyabhijñā: 'knowledge, memory, exclusion'."**

## 4. IPK LINKS
- **ĪPK 1.3.7** — THE kārikā: the one consciousness with jñāna-smṛti-apohana powers.
- **ĪPK 1.3.6** (from Ch2) — the synthesis argument that leads into 1.3.7.
- The three powers ↔ prediction (jñāna), retention (smṛti), selection (apoha) in active
  inference.

## 5. THESIS LITERATURE-REVIEW VALUE
- **The bearer** (Stage 2): the one consciousness that unifies. **The structure node.**
- **jñāna–smṛti–apohana** = the three operations of the predictive mind (Solms/neuro):
  this is the paper's most direct tradition↔science mapping.
- **aiśvarya = svātantrya**: sovereignty/freedom is the essence — the Ch7 theme begun here.

## 6. IPVV TRANSLATION HOOKS
- **maheśvara** (the great Lord) — the unifier.
- **jñānaśakti / smṛtiśakti / apohanaśakti** — the three powers (flag as the corrected triad).
- **aiśvarya / svātantrya** — sovereignty/freedom.
- **cittattva** (consciousness principle) — the Vṛtti's term for the all-forms unity.

*Ch3 is the corrected structure node: the bearer is the one consciousness with the three
powers jñāna-smṛti-apohana, and its essence is freedom (aiśvarya = svātantrya). Pair the

mislabel.*
